Jordan —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our legal/security team (cc'd Sally) reviewed the MSA redline and had a few clarifying questions before we sign the order form. Two items stood out:

1) Pen test / inspection scope: the current exhibit allows for "inspection and penetration testing" but doesn't define boundaries (internet-facing vs internal). Can you confirm whether Redwood expects full internal access or if you can live with internet-facing surface only?

2) Evidence cadence and SOC 2: we need a short-run runbook for how Redwood will provide SOC 2 evidence and pen-test results (frequency, point-of-contact, and data we should expect). Also, we need to understand whether Redwood will accept a scoped, time-boxed pen test with ephemeral creds rather than long-term privileged access.

We attached our preferred redline summary (inline comments) to the order form. High level ask: can you propose an evidence handoff timeline and a narrow pen-test scope that keeps PHI/IP internal networks out of scope?

Appreciate a short call if useful.

—Darwin
Head of Information Security, OmniHealth

For SOC 2 evidence we can provide a summary report and targeted artifacts (config screenshots, control evidence) on a quarterly cadence plus an annual assertion bundle.

Marissa — can you confirm the proposed evidence cadence below and attach the SOC 2 summary we usually share with prospects? Laura — flag any legal constraints on the redline language (we can propose edits to the exhibit to reflect scope limits).

- Evidence sprint: 10-business-day handoff window where we stage requested artifacts in a shared Drive folder
- Pen-test window: 5 business days notice; testing limited to agreed targets; ephemeral creds rotated daily; post-test debrief + remediation timeframe (30 calendar days)

Darwin — appreciate the detail. I reviewed the MSA redline and drafted an operational playbook below to make the legal language actionable for your ops team. Also attaching our SOC 2 top-line summary for 2025.

Operational playbook (proposed):
1) Pen-test scope definition
   - Default: internet-facing endpoints only (public API endpoints, web UI, ingress load balancers)
   - Optional: scoped staging environment by request (explicit targets agreed in writing)
   - Out-of-scope: internal-only networks, back-end databases containing PHI/PCI, and management plane unless explicitly authorized

2) Authentication & access
   - Testers provisioned ephemeral API keys / accounts that expire within the test window
   - No persistent elevated creds; any temporary SSH/RDP access must be pre-approved and time-limited

3) Notice & scheduling
   - Standard notice: 5 business days
   - For emergency or low-risk scans we can accept 48-hour notice with mutual written acknowledgement

4) Evidence cadence and handoff
   - SOC 2 summary: provided as PDF within 5 business days of request
   - Artifact sprint: pre-scheduled 10-business-day sprint where artifacts (logs, config screenshots, policy docs) are staged in a shared folder
   - Post-pen-test report: we will provide remediation notes within 10 business days; fix/mitigation target 30 days

5) Escalation & point-of-contact
   - Primary: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com) — security operations lead for evidence/scope
   - Contracts: Jordan Blake (jordan.blake@redwood.com) — order form/contract updates

I attached SOC2-2025-summary.pdf for your internal review. If OmniHealth wants a narrower test (internet-only), we can incorporate that language into the Order Form exhibit and move to signature quickly. If you need an explicit carve-out for certain endpoints, please mark them in the redline and we'll accept that as the binding scope.

Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
